patch.value: A declared context intent returns no context when combined with the narrowing flag, and its refusal receipt reports 122 tokens against a 2400 budget as the reason it does not fit

Measured 2026-08-16 on this tracker. pm context --for orient returns context (7832 bytes, ~1958 tok, under its declared 2400 ceiling). pm context --for orient --limit 10 returns no context at all: budget_exceeded.omitted_result true, reason declared_budget_infeasible. Adding the narrowing flag destroys the answer. The emitted receipt then reports estimated_tokens 122 against token_budget 2400 with within_budget false and declaration_feasible false, because the final updateContextIntentEstimate call in applyContextIntentProjection re-estimates over the refusal object it just built, overwriting the estimate that justified the refusal. The number shown is not the number compared. Both named recoveries are also wrong: narrowing the request is what caused the omission, and --token-budget 20000 still omits. --token-budget 200000 succeeds and emits estimated_tokens 132522 under an intent whose declaration is 2400, because an explicit budget replaces the declared ceiling rather than being bounded by it.

A refusal receipt reports the estimate that produced the refusal, never an estimate recomputed over the refusal itself, and a test asserts the reported estimated_tokens exceeds token_budget whenever result_omitted is true; Applying an explicit row bound to a declared intent never produces a smaller result set and a larger reported cost than the same intent without it; Recovery guidance for an infeasible declaration names a recovery that is verified to work on the corpus that produced the refusal, rather than a generic instruction; An explicit --token-budget above a declared intent ceiling either is refused, is clamped to the declaration, or emits an explicit receipt field stating that the declaration was overridden and by how much; A negative control proves each assertion fails when the defect is reintroduced
A declared intent bounds a read and reports honestly why, and narrowing the request never removes the answer.
context --for orient --limit 10 omits the result entirely and justifies it with a number 20x under the bound it claims to have exceeded.

value.text:
Reproduction, exact commands and observed bytes on this tracker at tree 9da5886cc:

  pm context --limit 10                              7,988 B  ~1,997 tok  result returned
  pm context --for orient                            7,832 B  ~1,958 tok  result returned, budget 2400
  pm context --for orient --limit 10                   520 B              RESULT OMITTED
  pm context --for orient --limit 50                   520 B              RESULT OMITTED
  pm context --for orient --token-budget 20000         521 B              RESULT OMITTED
  pm context --for orient --token-budget 200000    448,564 B  ~112k tok   result returned, receipt says estimated_tokens 132522
  pm context --for handoff                           4,588 B              result returned
  pm context --for handoff --limit 10                  524 B              RESULT OMITTED

The receipt for the omitted case, verbatim: token_budget 2400, estimated_tokens 122, within_budget false, declaration_feasible false, result_omitted true, degradation budget_receipt_only.

Three separable defects in one path: (1) the reported estimate is recomputed over the refusal so it contradicts the verdict it accompanies; (2) --limit turns a feasible intent infeasible on both declared context intents; (3) an explicit --token-budget replaces the declared ceiling instead of being bounded by it, so the same intent that declares 2400 emits 132522 with no field saying the declaration was overridden.

This is the fifth defect landed against the declared-intent layer after pm-ai45y9, pm-7hbfch, pm-prsvjh and pm-yekkvt. pm-yekkvt's AC4 already forbids recovery guidance that points at the unprojected command when that form is larger; here the unprojected form is SMALLER and succeeds, so the guidance is wrong in the direction that AC did not anticipate.
